title: A Smile for the Bell
premise: Emrys Lockridge, a pest controller with a habit of counting doors and keeping lights on, is hired to clear something out of Bellharrow, a decaying manor whose founders vanished mid-ritual two centuries ago. The house's mirrors begin reflecting each room one second late, and Emrys realizes the delay is widening — the house is pulling the present backward into the moment the ritual failed. To escape, Emrys must complete what the founders started, but finishing it means inheriting the house's hunger and becoming its next keeper. In the end, Emrys chooses to stay behind as the new bell-keeper, sealing the door from the inside so the last person out — a skeptical local historian who became their only ally — can leave with the truth.
about_author: Ines Marchetti is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent a decade cataloguing structural decay in inherited estates across the English countryside. Their fiction blends procedural precision with domestic dread, exploring how houses remember the people who fail to leave them.

chapters.title: The Callout Fee
chapters.summary: Emrys Lockridge takes a job at Bellharrow Manor after three previous pest controllers refuse it. POV: Emrys. They inventory the house obsessively — doors, lights, exits — establishing their coping rituals. Emotional beat: wary professionalism masking a lifetime of needing control over enclosed spaces.

chapters.title: Something With Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Emrys finds greasy handprints on the inside of sealed walls, too high to reach and too small for an adult. POV: Emrys. The client, estate lawyer Marguerite Voss, insists the infestation is rats. Emotional beat: creeping doubt — whatever made these prints wanted to be found.

chapters.title: Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Emrys counts eleven doors at dusk; by midnight there are twelve. The extra door is warm and breathes when pressed. POV: Emrys, with a flashback to childhood locked in a cellar. Emotional beat: old fear resurfacing, ritual counting failing them for the first time.

chapters.title: The Historian
chapters.summary: Local historian Sable Fenwick arrives uninvited, researching the founders' disappearance in 1804. She shows Emrys a portrait: five founders, one face smudged out. POV: alternating Emrys and Sable. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; Sable's skepticism cracks against Emrys's evidence.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Emrys notices a mirror reflecting the hallway a beat behind reality. Testing it, they wave; the reflection waves late. By morning every mirror lags. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: vertigo — the house is no longer just occupied, it is rehearsing.

chapters.title: What the Founders Started
chapters.summary: In the cellar, Sable deciphers the founders' ledger: a rite called the Keeping, meant to bind a guardian spirit into the house's bones. It was interrupted — the fifth founder fled. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: scholarly thrill curdling into horror as she realizes the rite needs a living keeper.

chapters.title: The Widening
chapters.summary: The mirror lag stretches to four seconds. Emrys watches their reflection finish a movement they haven't made yet — and it smiles first. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: loss of trust in their own body; the house is learning to be them.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Interest
chapters.summary: Voss returns, pressing Emrys to sign an 'inheritance contingency' clause. Her family name appears in the founders' ledger. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: her polished greed revealed as generational complicity — her line has been feeding keepers to Bellharrow for generations.

chapters.title: Rooms That Remember
chapters.summary: Wandering at night, Emrys enters a bedroom furnished in 1804, where the smudged founder's ghost relives her flight from the ritual. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: pity — the fifth founder didn't abandon the rite out of cowardice but mercy, refusing to trap anyone.

chapters.title: Pulled In
chapters.summary: The lag hits ten seconds; a mirror swallows Emrys into the reflected hall, a frozen copy of Bellharrow where the interrupted moment loops endlessly. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: terror of being stuck between seconds, and the discovery that the founders' shadows still pace here.

chapters.title: Sable Crosses Over
chapters.summary: Sable deliberately enters through the great mirror to find Emrys, armed with the ledger and salt. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: loyalty overriding reason — she'd rather be trapped with a friend than safe with a mystery.

chapters.title: The Looping Hour
chapters.summary: Inside the reflection, time runs in circles around the failed ritual. The founders' shades mistake Emrys for the missing fifth. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: belonging offered as a trap — the house wants to love them into staying.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Door
chapters.summary: Outside, Voss seals the manor and calls the family solicitors: the inheritance transfers if both intruders die inside. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: corruption completing itself — she believes she is honoring tradition, not committing murder.

chapters.title: Terms of the Keeping
chapters.summary: The house speaks through the mirrors: finish the ritual or dissolve into the loop. Emrys learns the rite requires a willing keeper bound to the bell in the tower. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: rage at the choice — freedom or servitude, nothing between.

chapters.title: The Fifth Founder's Confession
chapters.summary: The ghost of Ada Bellharrow explains how to unmake the rite instead of completing it — but it demands a keeper regardless; someone must hold the door forever. POV: Ada/Emrys shared scene. Emotional beat: grief across two centuries; mercy was never free.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Emrys performs their rituals one final time — every light burning, every door counted — turning coping into preparation, mapping the loop's seams. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: quiet resolve; their compulsions become weapons.

chapters.title: The Tower Bell
chapters.summary: Emrys and Sable fight through the looping house to the bell tower as the lag collapses toward zero. Voss's hired men breach the doors below and are taken. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; the house is eating the present.

chapters.title: Climax: Ring the Changes
chapters.summary: At the top, Emrys must ring the bell to seal the loop — binding themselves as keeper. Sable tries to take their place; Emrys tricks her through the collapsing mirror with the ledger as proof. The bell rings. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, corrupting power refused.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Smile
chapters.summary: Emrys becomes part of the house — not consumed but transformed, able to open the door for others. They guide Sable out and release Ada's shade at last. POV: Emrys, now half-house. Emotional beat: bittersweet transcendence; belonging achieved on their own terms.

chapters.title: After: The Empty Estate
chapters.summary: Sable publishes nothing, keeps the ledger hidden, and visits the silent manor monthly. Voss's inheritance dissolves — the deed lists no owner. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: haunted peace; some truths are kept like graves.

chapters.title: A New Callout
chapters.summary: Years later, a young pest controller gets a strange referral: a house that keeps its own lights on and counts its own doors. At the threshold, a warm presence checks her over like a colleague. POV: the newcomer. Emotional beat: eerie comfort — Emrys now protects people from houses like the one that took them.

chapters.title: Bellharrow Keeps Its Own
chapters.summary: Final chapter from inside the walls: Emrys walks the mirrored halls, no longer lagging, tending the loop like a garden, the bell humming above. Somewhere, a door opens for someone who needs it. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: acceptance — power contained, inheritance rewritten, belonging earned.
